problem_statement: The CBOR library must provide APIs to write and read signed integer values (cbor_write_signed / cbor_read_signed) in addition to the existing unsigned API.

verification.reason: The task can be made fair by adding the public prototypes and the observable encoding/error behavior of the signed APIs without prescribing the internal implementation.

problems.detail: The statement names cbor_write_signed/cbor_read_signed but does not give their prototypes or return types; the hidden test relies on cbor_write_signed taking int64_t and cbor_read_signed taking int64_t* and returning cbor_size_t.

The hidden test checks exact CBOR bytes and round-trip behavior for signed values, including non-negative values encoded like unsigned integers and negative values using the standard CBOR negative-integer major type; the statement does not specify this observable encoding.

The hidden test relies on cbor_read_signed returning CBOR_SIZE_NONE for non-integer or values not representable in int64_t and on supporting the full int64_t range including INT64_MAX/INT64_MIN; the statement does not specify these edge cases.

problem_statement_fixed: The CBOR library must provide APIs to write and read signed integer values (cbor_write_signed / cbor_read_signed) in addition to the existing unsigned API. The public functions should be `void cbor_write_signed(cbor_writer_state_t *state, int64_t value)` and `cbor_size_t cbor_read_signed(cbor_reader_state_t *state, int64_t *value)`. `cbor_write_signed` must encode non-negative values using the same encoding as the existing unsigned integer API and must encode negative values using the standard CBOR signed-integer major type. `cbor_read_signed` must accept items encoded with either the unsigned or the signed integer major type, return a `cbor_size_t` (using `CBOR_SIZE_NONE` for an error), and store the decoded value in `*value`. The new APIs must round-trip all `int64_t` values, including `INT64_MIN` and `INT64_MAX`.
